engine.label: Piper Kristin medium split decoder · sentences · 4 threads
engine.streaming: libpiper split voice: one encoder pass per part, then overlapping decoder chunks, so audio is incremental within a sentence; full mode drains the same chunks into one
engine.chunkPolicy: splitSentences: whole sentences, no carved first chunk; chunks are libpiper's decoder chunks (first 32 latent frames, 372 ms, 12 context frames each side, later 24 to 256 frames sized from decoder speed), untrimmed, no added gaps
engine.cancellation: between decoder chunks in the worker (no stop request yet; a host stops by not sending the next part, the current part runs to completion)

loadDetail.note: loadMs is the Piper Plus frontend (CMU dict parse) plus worker spawn and piper_create (encoder and decoder sessions)

If you are happy with that plan, I will schedule the production rollout for Friday morning, before the team meeting. Let me know if you would rather wait until next week, and I will move everything back.

I finished reading the three papers you flagged last night. The first one claims a forty percent speed up, but only on short prompts, and their test machine had twice our memory. The second paper is more useful: it shows that splitting text at commas cuts the wait before speech by about half. The third is mostly a survey, so I only kept the summary table. Overall, I think the comma trick is worth trying first, because it needs no new model and could ship in a day. I wrote up the details in the research folder, with links to each paper and the numbers I checked. Tell me if you want a shorter version for the team update on Monday.
